summary: This note describes the Solicitor General of India, the country's secondary law officer who sits below the Attorney General for India and assists them. It explains the appointment process, the three-year term, and the distinction that the Solicitor General's post is statutory rather than constitutional, unlike the Attorney General's post under Article 76. It also names Ranjit Kumar as the present Solicitor General, appointed on 7 June 2014.
one_line: Overview of the Solicitor General of India, the secondary law officer below the Attorney General, its appointment process, and its statutory status.
key_facts: The Solicitor General of India ranks below the Attorney General for India, who is the Indian government's chief legal advisor and primary lawyer in the Supreme Court of India.
The Solicitor General of India is appointed for a period of 3 years.
The Solicitor General of India is the secondary law officer of the country and is assisted by several Additional Solicitors General of India.
Ranjit Kumar is the present Solicitor General of India, appointed on 7 June 2014.
The Solicitor General and the Additional Solicitors General advise the Government and appear on behalf of the Union of India under the Law Officers (Terms and Conditions) Rules, 1972.
The post of Attorney General for India is a Constitutional post under Article 76 of the Constitution of India.
The posts of the Solicitor General and the Additional Solicitors General are merely statutory, not constitutional.
The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet appoints the Solicitor General of India.
The Attorney General for India is appointed by the President under Article 76(1) of the Constitution.
The Solicitor General is appointed to assist the Attorney General along with four Additional Solicitors General.
The proposal for appointing the Solicitor General or an Additional Solicitor General is generally moved at the level of Joint Secretary / Law Secretary in the Department of Legal Affairs.
After obtaining the approval of the Minister of Law & Justice, the proposal is sent to the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet for its approval.
